# Mergeway CLI - LLM Reference

This file is a high-signal reference for language models working with Mergeway CLI and authoring Mergeway workspaces.

Mergeway CLI manages structured metadata in Git-backed workspaces. It defines entity schemas in YAML or JSON Schema, loads YAML/JSON records from disk, validates structure and references, formats files deterministically, diffs logical data changes, exports snapshots, and can generate ERDs.

## Fast Mental Model

- The workspace root contains `mergeway.yaml`.
- Config files may `include` other YAML files; included files are merged into one logical config.
- `entities` defines the schema. Each entity is one object type.
- Records may live inline under `data:` or in external YAML/JSON files referenced by `include`.
- Reference fields are declared by setting a field `type` to another entity name, for example `author: User`.
- Validation runs in three phases: `format`, `schema`, `references`.
- Most CLI commands operate on files inside the workspace root. Some read paths outside the root, but write commands do not.

## Canonical Workspace Shape

```text
workspace/
  mergeway.yaml
  entities/
    User.yaml
    Post.yaml
  data/
    users/
      user-alice.yaml
    posts/
      launch.yaml
```

Minimal entry file:

```yaml
mergeway:
  version: 1

include:
  - entities/*.yaml
```

Rules:

- `mergeway.version` is currently `1`.
- Top-level config `include` entries are glob patterns relative to the file that declares them.
- Top-level config include patterns must match at least one file.

## Entity Definition

An entity definition must provide:

- `identifier`
- either `fields` or `json_schema`
- optionally `include`
- optionally `data`
- optionally `description`

Type names must start with an uppercase letter. Field and property names may contain letters, digits, `_`, and `-`.

Example native entity:

```yaml
mergeway:
  version: 1

entities:
  Post:
    description: Blog posts shown on the marketing site
    identifier: id
    include:
      - data/posts/*.yaml
    fields:
      id:
        type: string
        required: true
      title:
        type: string
        required: true
      status:
        type: enum
        enum: [DRAFT, PUBLISHED]
        required: true
      author:
        type: User
        required: true
      tags:
        type: Tag
        repeated: true
      metadata:
        type: object
        properties:
          created_at:
            type: string
          editor:
            type: User
```

Field shorthand is supported:

```yaml
fields:
  id: string
  title: string
```

Shorthand only sets `type`. It does not imply `required: true`.

## Identifier Semantics

`identifier` supports three forms:

1. String field name:

```yaml
identifier: id
```

2. Expanded mapping:

```yaml
identifier:
  field: id
  generated: true
  pattern: "^post-[0-9]+$"
```

3. Reserved `$path` value:

```yaml
identifier: $path
```

Notes:

- `generated: true` is advisory metadata for downstream tooling. The CLI still requires an explicit identifier when creating objects.
- `pattern` on `identifier` is enforced during schema validation.
- Identifiers can be string, integer, or number values when field-based.
- `$path` means the workspace-relative file path is the object ID, for example `data/notes/alpha.yaml`.
- `$path` only works when each file yields exactly one object.
- `$path` cannot be combined with inline `data`.
- `$path` rejects `items:` arrays and selectors that return multiple objects from one file.

## Native Field Semantics

Supported native field types:

- Primitive scalars: `string`, `integer`, `number`, `boolean`
- `enum`
- `object`
- another entity name, which means a reference
- a native reference union such as `User | Team`

Important corrections for LLMs:

- There is no native `type: ref`.
- There is no native `list[string]` syntax.
- Arrays are modeled with `repeated: true`.

Supported field attributes:

- `type`
- `required`
- `repeated`
- `description`
- `enum`
- `default`
- `format`
- `pattern`
- `unique`
- `properties` for object fields

Details:

- `required: true` means the field must be present unless a `default` value exists.
- `default` satisfies validation when the field is missing, but the CLI does not automatically write that value back into source files.
- `unique: true` requires values to be unique across objects of the same entity.
- `unique: true` is invalid when `repeated: true`.
- `pattern` is enforced for identifier fields and string-like fields.
- Runtime `format` validation currently recognizes `email`, `uri`, and `url`.
- Other format strings may still be stored in config, but they are not enforced by current runtime validation.

Native enum example:

```yaml
status:
  type: enum
  enum: [DRAFT, PUBLISHED]
  required: true
```

## Nested Properties

This is the most important syntax detail for LLMs editing Mergeway schemas.

Native nested objects are declared with `type: object` and `properties`.

Correct:

```yaml
metadata:
  type: object
  properties:
    created_at:
      type: string
    creator:
      type: string
```

Also correct for arrays of nested objects:

```yaml
contacts:
  type: object
  repeated: true
  properties:
    label:
      type: string
      required: true
    email:
      type: string
      format: email
      required: true
```

Incorrect:

```yaml
metadata:
  type: object
  fields:
    created_at: string
```

Rules:

- Object fields must define `properties`.
- `properties` is the only supported nested-schema key for object fields.
- Nested `fields:` inside a field is rejected by the config loader.
- Nested required validation uses dotted paths like `metadata.creator`.
- Repeated nested objects validate each array element against the same `properties` map.
- Unique object fields are allowed; uniqueness is checked on the normalized structured value.

Useful example: `https://github.com/mergewayhq/mergeway-cli/tree/main/examples/nested-fields`

## References and Reference Unions

Reference example:

```yaml
author:
  type: User
  required: true
```

Repeated reference example:

```yaml
tags:
  type: Tag
  repeated: true
```

Reference union example:

```yaml
owner:
  type: User | Team
```

Rules:

- A plain entity name in `type` means the field stores that entity's identifier.
- Repeated references are arrays of identifiers.
- Reference unions are only supported in native `fields:` definitions.
- A reference union value must resolve in exactly one target entity set.
- If the same identifier exists in multiple union targets, validation fails as ambiguous.
- Reference unions are not supported in `json_schema` entities.
- Reference unions cannot be exported by `mergeway-cli config export`.

Useful example: `https://github.com/mergewayhq/mergeway-cli/tree/main/examples/reference-union`

## JSON Schema Entities

Instead of native `fields`, an entity can point to a local JSON Schema document:

```yaml
entities:
  Customer:
    identifier: id
    include:
      - data/customers/*.json
    json_schema: schemas/customer.json
```

Rules:

- `json_schema` is resolved relative to the file that declares the entity.
- The JSON Schema file must live inside the repository.
- External `$ref` targets are rejected.
- In-document refs like `#/$defs/...` are supported.
- The root schema must describe an object.
- When `json_schema` is present, omit native `fields`.

Import behavior:

- JSON Schema `type: object` becomes a native object field with `properties`.
- JSON Schema `type: array` becomes `repeated: true` plus the item type.
- JSON Schema `enum`, `const`, and eligible `oneOf` blocks map to native enum fields.
- JSON Schema `x-reference-type` maps to Mergeway references.
- JSON Schema reference unions in `x-reference-type` are rejected.
- JSON Schema `description`, `format`, `pattern`, and `default` are imported.

Useful example: `https://github.com/mergewayhq/mergeway-cli/tree/main/examples/json-schema`

## JSON Schema Export

`mergeway-cli config export --type <Type>` exports a native Mergeway entity as JSON Schema.

Current export behavior:

- Primitive native fields become primitive JSON Schema properties.
- Native `enum` fields become JSON Schema string enums.
- Native object fields become JSON Schema objects with nested `properties`.
- Repeated fields become JSON Schema arrays.
- References become JSON Schema strings with `x-reference-type`.
- Required fields populate the JSON Schema `required` list.
- `description` is exported.

Current limitations:

- Reference unions are not exportable.
- Export does not currently emit every native validation rule. In particular, do not rely on export to preserve `pattern`, `format`, `default`, or `unique`.

Useful docs page: `https://mergewayhq.github.io/cli/cli-reference/config-export/`

## Data Sources

Entity `include` entries may be:

1. A glob string:

```yaml
include:
  - data/users/*.yaml
```

2. A mapping with `path` and optional `selector`:

```yaml
include:
  - path: data/users.json
    selector: "$.users[*]"
```

Meaning:

- A plain string is shorthand for `path` with no selector.
- Without a selector, Mergeway reads the whole file as one object.
- If the file contains an `items:` array, Mergeway uses those items as multiple objects.
- With a selector, each matched value must be an object.
- A selector that matches no values is an error.

Useful example: `https://github.com/mergewayhq/mergeway-cli/tree/main/examples/jsonpath`

## Inline Data

Entities may embed records directly:

```yaml
entities:
  Person:
    identifier: id
    fields:
      id:
        type: string
        required: true
      name:
        type: string
        required: true
    data:
      - id: person-1
        name: Alice
```

Rules:

- Inline data is optional.
- Inline data participates in read and validation flows.
- If the same identifier exists inline and on disk, the file-backed record wins.
- Inline data is read-only at runtime.
- Use `update` and `delete`, not `data update` or `data delete`.
- Entities using `identifier: $path` cannot define inline data.

## Data File Semantics

Data files may be YAML or JSON.

Top-level `type` in a data file is optional:

```yaml
type: Post
id: post-001
title: Launch Day
author: user-alice
```

Notes:

- The CLI usually infers type from the entity that included the file.
- If a top-level `type` is present and conflicts with the expected entity, the file is rejected.
- Before schema validation, Mergeway strips top-level `type` from the object payload.
- Numeric identifiers are allowed when the schema expects `integer` or `number`.

## Write and Read-Only Constraints

Create, update, and delete work on file-backed records inside the workspace root.

Important constraints:

- Selector-backed records are read-only for `create`, `update`, and `delete`.
- External-root `$path` records are also read-only through mutating commands.
- Those records can still be listed, fetched, validated, diffed, and exported.

## CLI Reference

Global flags available to all commands:

- `--root`: workspace root, default `.`
- `--config`: explicit config path, default `<root>/mergeway.yaml`
- `--format`: `yaml` or `json`
- `--fail-fast`: stop validation after the first error where supported
- `--yes`: skip confirmation prompts
- `--verbose`: enable extra logging

Command summary:

- `init`: scaffold a workspace with a starter `mergeway.yaml`
- `entity list`: list discovered entities
- `entity show <Entity>`: print the normalized entity definition
- `list --type <Type>`: list object identifiers
- `get --type <Type> <id>`: print one object
- `diff [<left>] [<right>]`: compare logical data snapshots; configuration changes are excluded
- `create --type <Type> [--file path] [--id value]`: create a record
- `update --type <Type> --id <id> [--file path] [--merge]`: replace or merge a record
- `delete --type <Type> <id>`: delete a record
- `export [Type...]`: export records as YAML/JSON, optionally to `--output`
- `fmt [files...]`: format data/config files using canonical field ordering
- `validate [--phase ...]`: run format, schema, and reference checks
- `config lint`: validate configuration only
- `config export --type <Type>`: emit JSON Schema for one native entity
- `gen-erd --path <file>`: write an ERD using Graphviz
- `version`: print semantic version, commit hash, and build date

Validation specifics:

- Successful validation prints `validation succeeded`.
- Validation errors are written in the selected output format.
- `mergeway-cli validate` exits non-zero when errors are found.
- Requesting the `references` phase implicitly includes the `schema` phase.

Formatting specifics:

- `fmt` follows schema field order, including nested object properties.
- `fmt --stdout` prints formatted output instead of rewriting files.
- `fmt --lint` exits non-zero if any target file is not already canonical.

- `https://github.com/mergewayhq/mergeway-cli/tree/main/examples/jsonpath`: selector-backed JSON records

## Authoring Guidance for LLMs

When generating or editing Mergeway configs:

- Prefer native references like `type: User`, not invented keywords.
- Use `repeated: true` for arrays.
- Use `type: object` plus `properties` for nested fields.
- Do not use nested `fields:` blocks inside a field.
- Do not use `list[...]` syntax unless the codebase explicitly adds support later.
- Keep reference unions out of `json_schema` entities and out of exported JSON Schema expectations.
- Treat `format` carefully: only `email`, `uri`, and `url` are currently validated at runtime.
- If you change schemas or data, run `mergeway-cli validate`.
- If you are unsure about nested object syntax, use the nested-fields example: `https://github.com/mergewayhq/mergeway-cli/tree/main/examples/nested-fields`
